steps.title: Migrate captured-path extents, unwritten conversion, and recursive freeing
verification: captured-path ladder covers indexed insertion, leaf split, root growth, and validated child/key ordering
unwritten conversion preserves data allocation and changes only required extent metadata claims
recursive truncate/destroy emits descendant-first after-images and revoke order with root collapse
Linux debugfs bmap comparison and Docker-backed e2fsck -fn cover fragmented depth-2 and depth-3 conversion fixtures
steps.notes: Depth-0 through bounded depth-3 unwritten conversion and bounded recursive truncate/destroy release are now host-verified. Recursive release validates depth/key ordering/cycles and reserved or overlapping physical ranges, emits descendant-first extent-node after-images, updates merged allocation metadata, and retains sorted revoke/deferred-free claims. A Docker debugfs fixture now creates a real depth-two unwritten tree, converts it through Tx after-images, recursively truncates it, compares its retained debugfs bmap, and passes e2fsck -fn. The same fixture now proves unlink -> destroy e2fsck cleanliness; a bounded depth-three mock proves recursive truncate revokes all descendant nodes. The full depth-two root carry is now host-verified: splitting a full leaf and parent produces four metadata-node claims and promotes the inode root to depth three. The deep planner now splits a full depth-three leaf and carries through full ancestors, including inline-root growth when bounded by the ext4 maximum depth. An ignored 3 GiB Docker/debugfs fixture now uses two Linux in-leaf insertions to make a depth-three parent full, then converts another near-full three-block unwritten leaf through Tx. The immutable plan claims two metadata-only nodes and emits five extent-node after-images through the parent carry before e2fsck -fn accepts it. Linux depth-three split/carry format evidence is complete; crash cuts remain pending. Do not add depth-specific runtime shortcuts.

steps.notes: Depth-two host runtime witnesses cover public truncate checkpointing of the retained leaf/allocation/inode after-images and MutationHandle retention of recursive destroy deferred-free claims. A depth-three host witness now drives public flush admission, ordered-data settlement, and checkpoint through the next metadata mutation before validating the converted leaf home. Ignored Docker runtime witnesses now build Linux-generated Tier 1 depth-two and depth-three-parent-carry fragmented unwritten images, mount the same file-backed images through the public mutation-journal path, flush an unwritten page, settle with chmod, and pass Linux e2fsck -fn. The depth-three fixture retains metadata_csum so it exercises the writable Tier 1 profile and carries a leaf split through a full parent. External extent-node metadata_csum tails are refreshed in plan_write_page. PageBacked retains file-page lifecycle, ext4 retains mutation planning and JBD2 staging, and Mount retains settlement. A6 remains open for crash-bound acceptance.
